_citation: Saito, K., Poland, A. I. & Munro, R. H. (1977), 'A study of the background corona near solar minimum', Solar Physics 55, 121-134. DOI:10.1007/BF00150879. ADS 1977SoPh...55..121S.
_transcription: Transcribed by hand from the ADS scan recorded in docs/sources/solar-corona.md (page numbers are the journal's). Values in parentheses in the paper are extrapolations outside the 2.5-5.5 R_sun data range and are flagged here with "extrapolated": true. The tests check Table II's N_e against the Table I coefficients (Eq. 4) and B_K+F = B_K + B_F to rounding.
_about: Skylab (HAO white-light coronagraph) data, May 1973 - February 1974: the declining phase of cycle 20, about two years before minimum (p. 122). Brightness in units of the mean brightness of the solar disk B_sun; N_e in cm^-3; r in solar radii. B_F = B - B_K (Sect. 3.3). Relative and absolute brightness errors about 20 % and 50 % near 2.5 R_sun, a factor 2 better near 5 R_sun (p. 126).

table1._source: p. 130, Table I: coefficients for pB(rho) = a1 rho^-b1 + a2 rho^-b2 (Eq. 2) and N_e(r) = c1 r^-d1 + c2 r^-d2 (Eq. 4), spherically symmetric, derived for 2.5-5.5 R_sun

_table2_source: p. 130, Table II: equatorial coronal background model. The last column (N_e of the Newkirk-Saito minimum equatorial model) is not extrapolated.
_table3_source: p. 131, Table III: spherically symmetric polar model and axisymmetric polar values. At 5.0 R_sun N_e, pB and B_K are in parentheses (extrapolated); B_K+F and B_F are measured.
